text: Hae Min Lee, 18, was last seen alive at Woodlawn High School at approximately 2:15 PM on January 13, 1999. She failed to pick up her young cousin from daycare around 3:15-3:30 PM.
Adnan Syed, 17, was Hae Min Lee's ex-boyfriend. They broke up in late December 1998. Hae had started dating Don Clinedinst.

Jay Wilds stated in his first police interview (Feb 28, 1999) that he was at Jenn Pusateri's house, received a call at approximately 3:45 PM, and drove to meet Adnan off of Edmondson Avenue at a strip where Adnan showed him Hae's body in the trunk.
Jay Wilds stated in his second police interview (March 15, 1999) that the trunk pop location was the Best Buy parking lot near the high school, not Edmondson Avenue.
Jay Wilds stated in his third police interview (April 13, 1999) that Adnan killed Hae in Patapsco State Park and that Adnan paid him to help.
Jay Wilds told his friend Chris that he was at a pool hall in Catonsville when Adnan called, and the trunk pop happened there.
Jay Wilds told his friend Tayyib that Adnan called Jay the day before asking for help. Jay agreed to help bury, not kill. They met at a gas station where Adnan showed him the body.

In a 2014 interview with The Intercept, Jay Wilds changed the trunk pop location to outside his grandmother's house, hours later than his trial testimony. He admitted to lying to police, lying in trial testimony, and lying about where he first saw Lee's body.

Five core claims remained consistent across all of Jay Wilds' versions: (1) Adnan killed Hae on January 13, (2) Jay was at Jenn's until around 3:40 PM, (3) Hae's car was initially at the Park and Ride, (4) Adnan went to track practice, (5) she was buried in Leakin Park.
AT&T cell phone records showed Adnan's phone pinging cell tower L689B, which covers Leakin Park, at 7:09 PM and 7:16 PM on January 13, 1999. Both calls were incoming calls.

The cover sheet of the fax AT&T sent to detectives stated: 'Outgoing calls only are reliable for location status. Any incoming calls will NOT be considered reliable information for location.' Both Leakin Park pings were incoming calls.

AT&T expert witness Abraham Waranowitz was never shown the AT&T disclaimer before his trial testimony. In 2015, he signed an affidavit stating the disclaimer was critical information he should have addressed, essentially retracting his testimony.

Asia McClain stated she spoke with Adnan Syed at the Woodlawn Public Library between approximately 2:15 PM and 2:36 PM on January 13, 1999. She was waiting for her boyfriend to pick her up due to a snow/ice event.
Asia McClain wrote two letters to Adnan in jail on March 1 and March 2, 1999, stating she remembered seeing him at the library during the critical time window.
Defense attorney Cristina Gutierrez never contacted Asia McClain, never investigated the library alibi, and never called her as a witness at either trial.
Adnan's palm print was found on the back cover of a Baltimore map book in Hae's car. The page showing Leakin Park was torn out.
Adnan's fingerprints were found on floral wrapping paper in the trunk of Hae's car.
Adnan was Hae's ex-boyfriend and had been in her car many times. Fingerprints on the map book and floral paper are consistent with prior presence, not necessarily criminal activity.
No DNA evidence from Adnan Syed was found on Hae's body, clothing, shoes, or rape kit. Advanced touch DNA testing in 2022 excluded Syed.
Fingerprints found on the rearview mirror of Hae's car did not match Adnan Syed. They were run through CODIS with no match to anyone in the system.

Hae's body showed frontal (anterior) lividity, meaning she was face-down for 8+ hours after death. She was found on her right side in a shallow grave. This contradicts a 7 PM burial on the day of death.
Prosecution argued Adnan murdered Hae between 2:15 and 2:36 PM, requiring her to be intercepted, driven to Best Buy, strangled, and placed in the trunk within 21 minutes.
The 3:32 PM call to Nisha lasted 2 minutes 22 seconds. Prosecution argued Adnan and Jay were together and Adnan put Jay on the phone with Nisha, proving they were together after the murder.

The Nisha call was the only call ever made to her before 7:30 PM on a school day from Adnan's phone. Nisha was on speed dial (one-touch dialing). Defense argued it was likely a butt dial. Nisha could not confirm the specific date of the call.
Jenn Pusateri testified Jay told her that same night that Adnan killed Hae. She said she helped Jay dispose of evidence including shovels and clothing.

In the 2019 HBO documentary, Jenn Pusateri stated: 'Jay obviously picks and chooses what he tells, and at this point it has created such a mess.' This undermines her earlier corroboration of Jay's testimony.

Kristi Vinson (Cathy) testified Jay and Adnan came to her apartment on January 13 before the police call about Hae. However, her class records show she had a Wednesday evening class, and the conference she referenced occurred on January 22, not January 13. She later stated the events definitely could not have happened on the 13th.

Coach Sye testified track practice ran from approximately 4:00 to 5:30 or 6:00 PM. If Adnan was at track by 4:00, the window to commit murder, show Jay the body, make the Nisha call, and get to track is extremely compressed.
Hae Min Lee's diary entries referenced Adnan's possessiveness and difficulty letting go after their breakup.
The 2022 motion to vacate identified two alternative suspects known at the time but not properly investigated or disclosed to defense. One suspect had threatened to kill Hae Min Lee.

Suspect 1 (Mr. S / Alonzo Sellers) was the person who found Hae's body in Leakin Park. He had a criminal record including exposure incidents. Hae's car was found near a residence connected to one of the suspects.

Suspect 2 (Bilal Ahmed) was Adnan's mentor at the mosque. He was later convicted of sexually assaulting five former dental patients and is serving 16.5 years. The motion stated one suspect had threatened to kill Lee.

Don Clinedinst, Hae's current boyfriend, claimed to be working at Hunt Valley LensCrafters from 9 AM to 6 PM on January 13. His alibi manager at that store was his own mother. His employee ID number on the timesheet was different from his usual ID.
Jay Wilds claimed Adnan called him from a pay phone at Best Buy after the murder. Investigation by Serial podcast could not confirm a pay phone existed at that Best Buy location.

Defense attorney Cristina Gutierrez was disbarred on May 24, 2001, by the Maryland Court of Appeals. She consented to disbarment citing health problems (multiple sclerosis). Multiple former clients filed complaints about mishandled funds. She died in 2004.
Analysis of Jay's police interviews suggests his testimony may have been coached to fit the cell phone records. His narrative shifted to match tower data that police had already obtained.
The weather on January 13, 1999 in Baltimore was cold with temperatures around 30-40 degrees Fahrenheit. There were reports of ice on some roads in the afternoon.
Woodlawn High School had approximately 1,800 students enrolled during the 1998-1999 school year. The school day ended at 2:15 PM.
Hae Min Lee drove a 1998 Nissan Sentra, gray in color. The car was found on February 28, 1999 at a vacant lot near 300 Edgewood Street.
Multiple students at Woodlawn reported seeing Hae in the hallways between classes on January 13. She appeared to be in normal spirits.
The Woodlawn Public Library was located approximately 0.3 miles from the high school. It was open until 8 PM on weekdays.
Adnan Syed was a member of the track team and the magnet program at Woodlawn. He was described by teachers as a bright student with no disciplinary issues.
Jay Wilds worked part-time at an adult video store. He was not a student at Woodlawn High School but knew many students through social connections.
Ramadan was observed during January 1999. Adnan stated he was attending mosque services with his family during evening hours.
The Baltimore County Police Department handled the initial missing person report. The case was later transferred to Baltimore City Homicide.
Stephanie was Jay Wilds' girlfriend and also a friend of Adnan's. January 13 was Stephanie's birthday, which is why Adnan allegedly lent Jay his car and phone so Jay could buy her a gift.
An anonymous caller contacted Baltimore police on February 12, 1999, suggesting they look at Adnan Syed in connection with Hae's disappearance. The caller's identity was never confirmed.
A classmate reported seeing a man matching Adnan's description at a gas station near Leakin Park around 6:30 PM on January 13. This sighting was never corroborated.
Police found a torn page from a notebook in Hae's car with phone numbers. One number belonged to a classmate who had no involvement in the case.

A convenience store clerk near Woodlawn reported a suspicious person buying shovels on the evening of January 13. The clerk could not identify the person and the purchase was never linked to the case.
Hae Min Lee had recently applied for a job at a local mall. Co-workers at the store reported she had mentioned feeling followed, but no specific person was identified.
A partial shoe print was found near the burial site in Leakin Park. It was a common Nike shoe size 10. It could not be matched to any specific individual.
Traffic cameras on Route 40 showed a gray sedan similar to Hae's Nissan at 3:45 PM heading east. The plates could not be read and the vehicle was never confirmed to be Hae's car.
A neighbor near Leakin Park reported hearing what sounded like digging around midnight on January 13-14. Police noted the report but could not determine its relevance.
